body.title: End the running state only on the running turn's own done, not on an informational line's
body.reproduction: 1. In the VS Code plugin, start a chat turn that takes a while, so the progress widget shows the working state and the send button is the Stop square. 2. While it runs, cause the chat to post an informational line: for example a queued message that was retried (the line 'the turn failed with overloaded; retrying (attempt 1 of 3)'), or a message queued into a chat other than the one shown (the note 'Running your queued message in …'). Expected: the turn is still running, so the widget keeps showing the working state and the button stays Stop. Observed: the widget goes idle and the button turns back into Send, though the turn continues and its output keeps arriving. Reproduced in the page test harness: after a 'turn-running' message, a 'turn-event' of kind done under another turn id ('queue-retry-x') changed the widget from 'progress' to 'progress idle' and the button from Stop to Send.
body.rootCause: The page's handler for 'turn-event' calls setRunning(false) and setIdle() for every event of kind done or error, whatever turn it belongs to. The host's postInfo and persistInfo post an informational line as an assistant-delta followed by a done event under the line's own turn id (queue notes, the give-up note, a refusal, the blocked-directory and batch notes, the retry line and the sign-in line). The page does not know which turn is the running one: its 'turn-running' message carries only a session id, so it cannot tell a running turn's done from an informational line's.
body.fixIntent: The page ends the running state (the idle widget and the Send button) only on the done or error of the turn it considers running; the done that closes an informational line leaves a running turn running. A turn that ends, or Stop, still ends it as today, and the informational lines still appear.
